skill.name: context-compression
skill.description: Guides agents through structured context compression for long-running sessions, including summary templates, trigger strategies, and evaluation probes.
skill.summary: Compress long agent sessions while preserving files, decisions, and next steps.

content.value_statement: Long AI sessions lose critical decisions, file changes, and next steps when context windows fill. This skill provides structured compression methods and evaluation probes for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Explains anchored iterative, opaque, and regenerative summary approaches.
Provides sections for intent, files, decisions, current state, and next steps.
Compares threshold, sliding window, importance-based, and task-boundary triggers.
Defines recall, artifact, continuation, and decision probes for evaluation.
Includes a Python evaluator for probe generation and heuristic scoring.
Summarizes benchmark dimensions and tradeoffs across compression methods.
limitations: The evaluator uses heuristic scoring and stubbed LLM judge calls.
Token estimation and fact extraction are simplified examples.
Benchmark values are reference guidance, not guaranteed results.
The skill does not install memory systems or telemetry.

use_cases.title: Maintain Long Debugging Sessions
use_cases.description: Compress session history while preserving errors, files, decisions, and next actions.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Summary Quality
use_cases.description: Create probes that test whether compressed context supports accurate follow-up work.

use_cases.title: Design Team Handoff Summaries
use_cases.description: Build repeatable summary sections for implementation plans and session transitions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Structured Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner compression of an active session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress this session into structured sections. Include intent, files changed, files read, decisions, current state, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Trigger Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for an agent workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a compression trigger strategy for a coding agent with long debugging sessions. Compare threshold, sliding window, and task-boundary options.

prompt_templates.title: Build Evaluation Probes
prompt_templates.prompt: Create probe questions to test whether a compressed summary preserves recall, artifact trail, continuation state, and decision rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Compression Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this compression design for tokens-per-task efficiency. Identify likely re-fetch costs, missing artifacts, and evaluation probes before implementation.

output_examples.input: A long debugging session has an authentication error, Redis investigation, configuration changes, and failing tests.
output: Session intent names the authentication failure and current goal.
Files changed and files read are separated for accurate continuation.
Next steps focus on remaining tests and staging validation.

output_examples.input: A team wants to compare two compressed summaries for follow-up quality.
output: Recall probes test original errors and technical facts.
Artifact probes check file tracking and change descriptions.
Decision probes verify that rationale and alternatives survived compression.

output_examples.input: A product team needs a compression policy for long Claude Code sessions.
output_examples.output: Recommended policy uses structured summaries, a sliding window, and probe reviews at major task boundaries.

best_practices: Optimize for tokens per completed task, not only tokens per request.
Keep explicit sections for files, decisions, state, and next steps.
Test compressed summaries with probes before using them in production.
anti_patterns: Compressing aggressively without checking re-fetch costs.
Using free-form summaries that omit file and decision tracking.
Treating lexical similarity as proof of usable context retention.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps agents preserve useful working context when long sessions exceed context limits.

faq.question: Does it run external commands?
faq.answer: No. The included Python file provides local evaluation utilities and documentation examples.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What compression method does it recommend first?
faq.answer: It favors anchored iterative summarization when file tracking and decisions matter.

faq.question: Can it evaluate summary quality?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes probe-based checks for recall, artifacts, continuation, and decisions.

faq.question: Is it ready as a production service?
faq.answer: No. The evaluator is a reference implementation and needs production model calls and tokenizers.
